chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When Allah has no need for a servant, He tests him with stinginess.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reason behind a person becoming stingy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this chain from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys a saying of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) linking spiritual neglect to material constraint. The phrase 'had not Allah a need for him' (illa an yakuna li-llahi fihi hajatan) is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating that when Allah does not actively guide or sustain a servant's heart, He allows stinginess to manifest as a test or consequence of that spiritual disconnection. This highlights the reciprocal relationship between divine attention and the purification of character, where lack of divine focus leads to the accumulation of worldly goods without spiritual benefit.
